title: Democrats win 56 Senate seats and a large House majority as Alaska's Peltola wins the last Senate race
seoTitle: US midterm results 2026: Democrats 56 Senate seats, 257 House
dek: AP called Alaska for Democrat Mary Peltola on 17 November, giving Democrats 56 Senate seats after nine flips. In the House they have 257 seats with seven races uncalled, AP figures show.
happened: In the 3 November elections Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Republicans went in with a 53-47 Senate majority; Democrats will enter 2027 with 56 seats after flipping nine: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Mississippi, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas. Alaska was the last Senate race decided: AP called it late on 17 November for Mary Peltola over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. She took just over 50% of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice count was needed, and becomes the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alaska since 2008. In the House, AP figures give Democrats 257 seats, including 46 flipped from Republicans, with seven races uncalled; 218 is a majority. Their national House vote lead is about 14 points, the largest in a midterm since 1974 according to the Cook Political Report. Democrats also hold 30 governorships after flipping six (Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas), their first majority since 2011.

sides.says: After the election Trump signalled he would work with Democrats. Vice President JD Vance wrote: "The reason we lost is the war", meaning the war with Iran. Rep. Don Bacon said Stephen Miller, whom Trump named White House chief of staff, had "greatly hurt the administration and cost us many seats on Tuesday". In Alaska, Trump claimed Sullivan would win if the votes of a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan were added to his; Alaska Public Media says that is not true as the count stands, because Peltola's lead is more than double that candidate's total.

Peltola wrote: "Thank you, Alaska. Let's get to work." House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called Miller "a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist" and said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth "abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran". Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump "learned nothing from his historic defeat".

The Justice Department sued to block certification if Sullivan lost narrowly; a federal judge dismissed the suit, and Democracy Docket reports the administration has appealed. An investigation alleged that Peltola aides recruited the second Dan Sullivan to draw votes from the senator; Peltola denies any knowledge. Al Jazeera reports Sullivan pledged to accept the outcome; Democracy Docket reports his campaign said it would not concede at least until the result is certified.

next: Alaska's results are due to be certified on 25 November. Seven House races are uncalled, including Louisiana's 5th and 6th districts, which go to a 12 December runoff, and close counts in Minnesota's 1st (a recount is likely) and North Carolina's 5th and 10th (the Democratic candidate in the 10th has requested a recount); North Carolina certifies on 24 November and California on 11 December. The new Congress is sworn in early in January; Republicans keep control until then.
summary: Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterms. With Mary Peltola's win in Alaska, called by AP on 17 November, they have 56 Senate seats after flipping nine, and AP figures give them 257 House seats with seven races uncalled. They also hold a majority of governorships for the first time since 2011. Vice President Vance blamed the war with Iran for the losses. Alaska certifies its result on 25 November amid Republican challenges, and the new Congress takes over in early January.
